newsitem.title: GERMANY: Witness says Lebanese admitted fatal German arson.
newsitem.headline: Witness says Lebanese admitted fatal German arson.

text.p: A young Lebanese man confessed to an ambulance man that he started a fire in a refugees' hostel last January in which 10 people died, a German court heard on Monday.

The first aid worker, Jens Leonhardt, told the court that Safwan Eid, who denies charges of aggravated arson and causing bodily harm, poured out his heart on the night of the fire as if relieved to have someone to talk to.
"The words simply burst out of him...I had the impression that at last he had found someone to talk to," said Leonhardt, the prosecution's chief witness. "He told me: "It was us.'"

The fire was the worst disaster to hit a foreigners' home in Germany, and at first raised fears of a new wave of neo-Nazi racist violence similar to one which swept across the country after unification in 1990.
But police arrested Eid, a civil war refugee who lived in the hostel with his family for six years, on suspicion of trying to get revenge in a petty quarrel with another resident.
Leonhardt, who treated Eid for burns, only went to police after a fellow first aid worker encouraged him to come forward.
He said he could not remember the precise words Eid used, but said Eid described pouring petrol or another liquid outside a neighbour's door and setting it alight.
He said he warned Eid that such remarks could cost him dear. But the Lebanese appeared unmoved by his words. "I guessed he was still in shock," the ambulance man said.
Eid, who denies the charges, told the court last week the first-aider misheard him and that what he really said was: "It was them" -- meaning it was a racist attack by neo-Nazis.
The fire killed six people from Zaire, a man from Benin, a Lebanese and a woman from Angola and her six-year-old daughter. Thirty-eight people were injured.
Eid could face life imprisonment if convicted.

He gave his age as 20, which means he could be treated as a juvenile at the court's discretion and face a maximum 10-year sentence. But prosecutors say he was 21 at the time of the fire and must face a full adult penalty.
